title: Another school's Abhidharma
hookLine: the Sarvastivada school had its own Abhidharma, summarized by Vasubandhu
last: A PERSON IS A WAY OF SPEAKING, NOT AN EXTRA THING.

lines: ITS OWN BOOKS, ITS OWN LISTS.
cards: Yesterday's book argued with other schools without naming them. One of those schools had a name that is itself a claim: Sarvastivada, the teaching that all exists.
You met it among the eighteen schools on day eight hundred fifty-six. And it didn't only argue. It built its own Abhidharma, its own books, its own lists of what the world is made of.
For weeks this path has been learning one map of the mind. Today, a second map, drawn by people studying the same teacher, with the same care, from a different starting point.

teach.b: The Sarvastivadins held that the basic building blocks of experience, which they called dharmas, exist in the past, the present and the future, not only in this moment. That's where the name comes from.

It let them explain how a past deed can still bear fruit, or how memory reaches something gone. The Theravada side, as yesterday's book shows, answered that the past is past. Both were working from the Buddha's words.

This school's Abhidharma was gathered and argued over at length, then summed up by a monk named Vasubandhu in a book of verses called the Abhidharmakosha, the treasury of Abhidharma. Then something unusual.
Vasubandhu wrote his own commentary on those verses, and at points he raises objections to the very school he was summarizing, at times speaking for another group, the Sautrantikas.
A textbook that argues with itself in the margins. Now set the two lists side by side. The Theravada manual sorts everything into four: mind, mental factors, matter and nibbana.
The Treasury sorts it into five groups: matter, mind, mental factors, things that are neither matter nor mind, and the unconditioned. One small example: space.
In the Theravada manual, space is counted as a kind of matter, the gap that marks where one thing ends. In the Treasury, space is listed among the unconditioned.
Same space, two careful answers. The Treasury has been studied in other Buddhist traditions too, tradition says. Neither list is a rough version of the other.
They're two schools looking hard at the same world.

how: Students of Buddhist philosophy read Vasubandhu's Treasury of Abhidharma alongside the Theravada manuals, and some Mahayana monastic curricula include it as a core text.

o: the Buddha's lost lists, found centuries later
an early rough version of the Theravada lists
the Sarvastivada's own map of mind and matter

p: summed it up in the Treasury

s: the Sarvastivadins held that dharmas exist in past, present and future
that's the meaning of the name: the teaching that all exists.
Vasubandhu's commentary defends his school on every point
at points he raises objections to the school he was summarizing.
both lists put space in the same place
the Theravada manual counts it as a kind of matter; the Treasury lists it among the unconditioned.

games.q: you're Vasubandhu. you've written verses summing up a school's Abhidharma. now you sit down to write your own commentary on them. what do you do?
o: at points, raise objections to the school you summarized
games.why: his commentary at points argues with the very school his verses summarize, at times from the Sautrantika side: a textbook arguing in its own margins.

practice: Bring to mind two ways of doing the same ordinary thing, like two people who load a dishwasher or pack a bag differently, and hold both pictures side by side, noticing what each one gets right.
When the mind starts to pick a winner, notice that too and set it down. Let the two sit next to each other, both whole.

wordCard.voice: Another school's Abhidharma. The Sarvastivada map of mind and matter, summed up in Vasubandhu's Treasury, sorting the world into five groups. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the teaching that all exists, the name of an early Buddhist school with its own Abhidharma.

carryVoice: Your line: another school's list. Same world, two maps, and neither one a rough version. See you tomorrow.
